name: devdesk-claude
description: Claude Code sessions in tmux that keep running when VS Code closes, a Claude Board, and worktree diffs for git repositories, locally or over Remote-SSH.

scripts.package: npm run build && mkdir -p dist && vsce package --no-dependencies --skip-license --no-rewrite-relative-links -o dist/devdesk-claude.vsix

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Claude sessions are running.
[New Claude session](command:devdesk.sessions.new)
[New worktree session](command:devdesk.sessions.newWorktree)
[Show Claude Board](command:devdesk.board.open)

commands.title: New Claude Session in This Worktree
Open Next Claude Session Needing Input
Prompt for Later on Claude Board
Show Claude Plan Limits (Install DevDesk's Status Line)
Claude Terminal: ← (Focus the Claude View on an Empty Prompt)
Teach Claude the devdesk Command (Install Skill)

view/item/context.when: (view == devdesk.features && viewItem =~ /^feature/) || (view == devdesk.sessions && !listMultiSelection && viewItem =~ /^session\b/) || (view == devdesk.features && viewItem =~ /^session\b/)

enumDescriptions: Only Claude sessions running on DevDesk's tmux server (devdesk.sessions.tmuxServer).
Every Claude session on this machine: other tmux servers, plain terminals, IDE integrations and background jobs.
devdesk.sessions.show.description: Which Claude sessions the Claude view lists.

enumDescriptions: Only sessions working in this window's workspace: its root folder or one of its worktrees.
Sessions of every folder, also those started from other VS Code windows.
devdesk.sessions.scope.description: Which folders' Claude sessions the Claude view and the Claude Board list.

devdesk.sessions.groupByWorktree.markdownDescription: The Claude view nests sessions under their worktree. Off: it lists every session in one list, in attention order, each row naming its worktree. Toggle it with the Claude view's list button.

enumDescriptions: What needs you first: needs you (question, permission, plan, input, blocked; the longest waiting first), unread turns finished in the last few minutes (devdesk.sessions.recentlyFinishedMinutes), working, stuck, then read or older finished ones, not running and parked; newest first within each.
The order from before: needs input, blocked, unread done, working, read done, idle, then the rest, newest first; devdesk.sessions.unreadFirst puts unread sessions above read ones.
devdesk.sessions.sort.description: How the Claude view and the Claude Board order Claude sessions: in each worktree, in the flat list, and in each board lane.

devdesk.sessions.recentlyFinishedMinutes.markdownDescription: With `#devdesk.sessions.sort#` `urgency`: a Claude session whose turn finished less than this many minutes ago, and that you haven't read, sorts above working sessions.

devdesk.sessions.unreadFirst.markdownDescription: With `#devdesk.sessions.sort#` `attention`: sort unread Claude sessions above every read one. When off, unread sessions only sort first within their state (needs input, blocked, working, ...).

devdesk.sessions.dimRead.description: Grey the titles of Claude sessions you have read, so unread ones stand out in the Claude view.

devdesk.sessions.unreadBadge.description: Show a ● badge at the end of unread Claude session rows in the Claude view.

devdesk.sessions.notifyWhenWaiting.description: Show a notification when a Claude session starts waiting for you.

devdesk.sessions.statusBar.description: Show a status bar item with the number of Claude sessions needing input; click it to open the next one.

devdesk.sessions.stuckMinutes.description: A working Claude session with no progress (no hook event) for this many minutes shows as stuck (orange watch).

devdesk.sessions.hooksQuietMinutes.markdownDescription: A session whose status hooks have said working or waiting, with no new hook event, for this many minutes shows the state Claude itself reports instead, when it differs (it needs `#devdesk.sessions.programStatus#`). This catches a hook event that got lost, such as a permission you denied with Esc. 0: the hooks' state always wins.

devdesk.sessions.idleMinutes.description: A finished Claude session not updated for this many minutes sorts after working and recently finished sessions (it still shows as done).

devdesk.sessions.resortWorkingMinutes.description: Working Claude sessions keep their order in the Claude view and on the Claude Board for this many minutes, then sort again (newest first), so rows don't move each time a session does something. A session that starts working goes first among them. 0: always sorted.

devdesk.sessions.readAfterSeconds.description: A Claude session shows in bold (unread) when anything happened in it since you last looked; its terminal must be in front for this many seconds to count as read.

devdesk.sessions.finishedSessions.markdownDescription: How many parked (not running) Claude sessions the Claude view lists per worktree, and the Claude Board under the Idle / stopped divider of its Done / idle lane, newest first (unread ones stay above the divider and aren't counted); older ones fold into one `N earlier finished` row. They are listed until you remove them or Claude Code deletes their transcript (its `cleanupPeriodDays`, 30 days by default).

devdesk.sessions.showChildren.description: List what each Claude session spun off under its row: subagents (and their own subagents and shells), background shell commands, and workflows with their phases and agents. Read from the session's transcript.

devdesk.sessions.finishedChildren.markdownDescription: How many finished subagents, shells and workflows the Claude view lists per level; older ones fold into one `N earlier finished` row. Running ones are always listed. Applies when `#devdesk.sessions.showChildren#` is on.

devdesk.sessions.pollSeconds.description: How often (seconds) the Claude Sessions panel re-checks tmux while it is open or notifications are on.

devdesk.sessions.turnChangesTurns.markdownDescription: How many of a session's latest turns **Show Changes by Turn…** lists (read from the end of its transcript).

devdesk.sessions.turnChangesMaxMB.markdownDescription: How much (MB) of the end of a session's transcript, and of each of its subagents', **Show Last Turn's Changes** and **Show Changes by Turn…** read at most. Turns that started before it are listed as partly read.

enumDescriptions: Claude's own default (your settings' defaultMode)
--permission-mode manual: ask before every tool that needs permission
--permission-mode acceptEdits: edit files without asking
--permission-mode auto: a classifier approves safe actions
--permission-mode plan: read and plan only, no changes
--permission-mode dontAsk: deny anything not pre-approved, never prompt
--dangerously-skip-permissions: skip all permission checks
devdesk.sessions.defaultMode.markdownDescription: The `#devdesk.sessions.modes#` entry every new Claude session starts in (+, the robot icon on a worktree, Fork). The list offers the modes DevDesk ships; to start in a mode you added, type its name in settings.json (it works despite the warning). An unknown name uses the first mode.

name.description: Name shown in New Claude Session with Mode… and used by devdesk.sessions.defaultMode.

args.description: Claude Code arguments for this mode, in shell syntax.

default.name: Manual
default.description: Ask before every tool that needs permission

default.name: Plan
default.description: Read and plan only, no changes

default.name: Don't ask
default.description: Deny anything not pre-approved, never prompt

devdesk.sessions.modes.markdownDescription: Ways to start Claude Code. **New Claude Session with Mode…** and **Fork Claude Session with Mode…** list them (plus **Custom…** for one-off arguments); `#devdesk.sessions.defaultMode#` picks the one + and the robot icon use. Add your own, for example `{ "name": "Opus plan", "args": "--model opus --permission-mode plan --effort high" }`.

devdesk.sessions.claudeArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments for Claude Code in every new Claude session, whatever its mode, in shell syntax, for example `--model opus`. The launch mode's arguments (`#devdesk.sessions.defaultMode#`) come after these. Empty: none. Applies to sessions started after the change; `#devdesk.sessions.command#`, when set, replaces the whole command.

name.description: The account's name, shown in the board's account pill and on its sessions' cards.

configDir.description: Claude Code's config directory for the account (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): its login, settings, transcripts. A leading ~ is your home directory.

env.description: More environment variables the account's sessions start with.

devdesk.claude.accounts.markdownDescription: Claude accounts (profiles): each a `name` and a Claude Code config directory (`configDir`, given to Claude as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), with optional `env` for its sessions. With more than one, the Claude Board's composer has an account pill and **New Claude Session** asks which; a resumed or forked session keeps its account. An account whose `configDir` is Claude's own (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`) starts without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Empty: one account, Claude's own config directory.

devdesk.claude.defaultAccount.markdownDescription: The Claude account (a `name` in `#devdesk.claude.accounts#`) new sessions use unless you pick another. A folder's workspace settings can set its own. Empty: the first account listed.

devdesk.claude.disableAutoUpdater.markdownDescription: Claude sessions DevDesk starts run with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, so Claude Code does not update itself.

devdesk.sessions.claudePath.markdownDescription: Claude Code binary DevDesk starts in new Claude sessions. Empty: `$HOME/.toolbox/bin/claude` when it exists, else `claude` on PATH.

devdesk.sessions.command.markdownDescription: Full shell command tmux runs when it creates a feature's Claude session, overriding `#devdesk.sessions.claudePath#` and `#devdesk.sessions.claudeArgs#`. Empty: `<claudePath> <claudeArgs>; exec $SHELL -l`.

devdesk.sessions.programStatus.markdownDescription: Start new Claude sessions under DevDesk's Program Status relay (`python3`, `~/.claude/devdesk/devdesk_status.py`). It answers Claude Code's status probe (OSC 7501, Claude Code 2.1.295 or later), which tmux can't, so Claude reports whether it is working, waiting for an approval or an answer, or at its prompt. Sessions without status hooks then show that state, and sending to a session checks it instead of only reading the screen. Not used with `#devdesk.sessions.command#`. Applies to sessions started after you change it.

devdesk.sessions.restoreTerminals.markdownDescription: When a window opens (after a reload, or a Remote-SSH reconnect that restarted VS Code on the remote machine), reopen the Claude terminals that were open, attached to their tmux sessions. Sessions that ended in the meantime are skipped. Off: Claude terminals don't come back; open them from the Claude view.

devdesk.sessions.leftArrowOpensSidebar.markdownDescription: In DevDesk's Claude terminals, ← on an empty prompt focuses the Claude view (on that session's row) instead of opening Claude's agent view, and new Claude sessions start without agent view (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1`, which also turns off `/background` and `--bg`). DevDesk adds its ← command to `#terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell#` while this is on, and removes it when you turn this off.

devdesk.sessions.parkAfterDays.markdownDescription: Park a Claude session DevDesk started that has done nothing for this many days (fractions work): its tmux session and Claude process end, freeing their memory, and its row stays, marked parked. Opening it resumes the conversation (`claude --resume`), and a terminal tab that was open on it comes back with it. Sessions whose terminal is open, that wait on you or that still run subagents or shells are never parked. The settings below park sooner. `0`: never park (also turns off the settings below).

devdesk.sessions.parkReadAfterMinutes.markdownDescription: Park sooner, after this many minutes without activity, a finished session you have read whose last turn neither ended on an error nor asks you a question. Unread sessions wait for `#devdesk.sessions.parkAfterDays#`. `0`: only `parkAfterDays`.

devdesk.sessions.maxLiveSessions.markdownDescription: Keep at most this many DevDesk Claude sessions running: when more run, park the ones idle for `#devdesk.sessions.idleMinutes#`, read ones and the least recently active first. Working sessions, those waiting on you and those with an open terminal keep running, so more may run. Each running session takes memory (Claude and its MCP servers). `0`: no limit.

devdesk.sessions.parkBelowFreeMemoryPerc.markdownDescription: While less than this percent of the machine's memory is free (`MemAvailable` on Linux, the memory pressure level on macOS), park one more session idle for `#devdesk.sessions.idleMinutes#` each minute, the least recently active first. `0`: never.

devdesk.sessions.tabTitleLength.markdownDescription: A Claude terminal's tab shows its session's board title (a `/rename`, else DevDesk's short title, else Claude's title or the prompt), cut to this many characters; until there is a title, the session's name (`main-39`). When the title changes, the tab follows the next time it is in front. `0`: always the session's name.

devdesk.worktrees.root.description: Workspace root: a git repository. Empty: the git repository containing the first workspace folder (its main worktree; a linked worktree resolves to it), else that folder as it is. The Claude and Worktrees views are hidden when no local folder is open.

devdesk.worktrees.showSessions.description: List each worktree's Claude sessions under its row, above its packages, as the Claude view shows them. Toggle it with the Worktrees view's comment button.

devdesk.worktrees.showCleanPackages.description: List the packages of a worktree that have no changes (shown as clean). Off: only changed packages are listed.

devdesk.worktrees.refreshSeconds.description: While the Worktrees view is visible, refresh it this many seconds after the previous refresh finished (a refresh never starts while one is running). 0 disables.

devdesk.worktrees.pauseWhenUnfocused.description: Pause the Worktrees view's refresh while the VS Code window is in the background. Coming back refreshes at once if the last refresh is older than devdesk.worktrees.refreshSeconds.

devdesk.worktrees.activeReloadSeconds.description: The packages of a worktree that is expanded, or that a Claude session is busy in, load again at least this often (seconds), for edits git has not seen yet. Saves in VS Code, Claude's edits, a finished Claude turn, commits, checkouts and `git add` reload a package at once. 0: only those.

devdesk.worktrees.idleReloadMinutes.description: The other worktrees' packages load again about this often (minutes), for edits git has not seen yet. They are spread over the refreshes, a few at a time, so one may load up to half an interval later. 0: only when a save, a Claude edit or a git change says they changed.

devdesk.worktrees.prefetch.description: While the Worktrees view is visible, load every worktree's changes in the background (after the expanded ones), so expanding a worktree shows them at once and each row shows how many packages changed.

devdesk.worktrees.maxGitProcesses.description: The most git processes the Worktrees view runs at once. An expanded worktree's packages may use all of them; background loads (prefetching every worktree) use up to half, or a quarter while the machine is busy (load average above 1.5 per CPU), and at least one.

devdesk.worktrees.gitTimeoutSeconds.description: Stop a git command of the Worktrees view that runs longer than this (seconds); its package shows an error instead of the view loading forever. 0 never stops it.

devdesk.worktrees.startPrompt.markdownDescription: Claude's first prompt in a new worktree session: `{task}` is what you typed, `{worktree}` the worktree name, `{dir}` its directory. Empty: `You are working in worktree {worktree} ({dir}) on: {task}`, followed by asking Claude to say which worktree it is in and start on the task.

devdesk.worktrees.cleanupIdleDays.markdownDescription: **Clean Up Worktrees…** lists only worktrees with no commit, checkout or rebase for this many days.

devdesk.worktrees.cleanupBaseBranches.markdownDescription: Branches a worktree's commits must be in (any of them, compared by patch: rebased and cherry-picked commits count as in, squash-merged ones do not) for **Clean Up Worktrees…** to list it, for example `["main", "release"]`. Empty: each package's mainline (`origin/mainline`, `origin/HEAD`, `main`, …, the first that exists).

devdesk.worktrees.cleanupDeleteBranch.markdownDescription: **Clean Up Worktrees…** also deletes a git worktree's branch (all its commits are in a base branch). Off: the branch stays, like **Delete Worktree** leaves it.

devdesk.worktrees.cleanupSuggestCount.markdownDescription: When a window opens and at least this many worktrees are ready to clean up, DevDesk offers **Clean Up Worktrees…** (it never deletes on its own). `0`: never offer.

devdesk.worktrees.autoTrust.markdownDescription: Accept Claude's *Do you trust the files in this folder?* for a worktree DevDesk makes (New Worktree Session, the board, `devdesk worker start`), so its session starts without asking. Only when Claude already trusts the workspace (or repository) it is made in, and only for the worktree and its packages: DevDesk writes `hasTrustDialogAccepted` for them in Claude's config file (`#devdesk.board.claudeConfigFile#`). In a package Claude has not trusted, DevDesk then makes a Claude Code worktree with `git worktree add` from `HEAD` (`claude --worktree` refuses to start there). Off: Claude asks, and the session opens so you can answer.

devdesk.board.openWhenEmpty.markdownDescription: Open the Claude Board when the editor area has no tabs (when the window starts and when you close the last tab, unless that tab was the board).

devdesk.board.openWithSidebar.markdownDescription: Open the Claude Board the first time you open the Agent Sessions sidebar in a window, so it is what the sidebar starts on.

devdesk.board.editorTitleButton.markdownDescription: Show a colored Claude Board button at the top right of each editor group (next to the editor actions, such as Claude Code's), that opens the board.

enumDescriptions: In a square of its own under the lanes, its top edge in the mode's colour; it grows up into the board for a long prompt
In the same square above the lanes, its bottom edge in the mode's colour; it grows down into the board for a long prompt
devdesk.board.promptPlacement.markdownDescription: Where the Claude Board's prompt box sits.

devdesk.board.sidebarPrompt.markdownDescription: Show the **New Session** view above the Claude view: the Claude Board's prompt box (the same choices, `/` commands, `@` files and pasted images), to start a session without opening the board.

enumDescriptions: Stay on the board: the session starts in the background and its card shows in Working; open it from there
Open the new session's terminal
devdesk.board.afterStart.markdownDescription: What happens after the Claude Board's prompt box starts a session (Enter, or **Start** / **Plan** / **Spec** on a prompt for later).

enumDescriptions: Beside the board when the editor area is wide enough for the full board and a terminal at least as wide
Beside the board, however wide the editor area (the board takes at most half)
Over the board, in its editor group
devdesk.board.sessionsBeside.markdownDescription: Where a session opened from the Claude Board shows its terminal when the board has the editor area to itself: beside it, the board keeping room for every lane (`#devdesk.board.laneWidth#`) and the terminal taking the rest, or over it. Once a Claude terminal is open in an editor group, the next ones open there.

devdesk.board.cardLine.markdownDescription: Show one line under the title of Working cards (what Claude is doing now) and Needs you cards (what Claude asks or wants approved). The ☰ button in the board header turns it on or off. The card's hover always shows both.

enumDescriptions: What the whole session sets out to do (its goal and tasks, from DevDesk's insights), with the latest step in smaller text under it.
What the latest prompt is about.
devdesk.board.cardTitle.markdownDescription: What the title of a session's card on the Claude Board says. `objective` (a prototype) needs `#devdesk.insights.enabled#`; until a session's objective is known its card shows the latest prompt's title. A name given with /rename always wins.

devdesk.board.laneWidth.markdownDescription: How wide (px) each of the Claude Board's lanes is when a session opens beside the board (`#devdesk.board.sessionsBeside#`): wider shows more of each card's summary, and the terminal gets less.

devdesk.board.models.markdownDescription: Models the Claude Board's prompt box offers, first one preselected: aliases (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) or full model names, passed as `--model` to the next session it starts. `Default` adds no `--model` (your Claude settings' model). Empty: the Claude CLI's own model list, else `Default`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`, `opus[1m]`, `sonnet[1m]`, `fable[1m]` when the CLI does not answer.

devdesk.board.specPrompt.markdownDescription: What **Spec** on a prompt for later puts before the prompt: a skill or command (`/name`, on the same line) or an instruction (on its own lines). Empty: `/superpowers:brainstorming` when that skill is installed and enabled, else *Before changing any code, write a design spec for the following and wait for my review of it.*

devdesk.board.pastedImagesDir.markdownDescription: Folder where images pasted into the Claude Board's prompt box are saved (the prompt mentions each with `@`, so Claude reads it). Pasted images older than 30 days are deleted from it. Empty: `~/.claude/devdesk/pasted-images`.

devdesk.board.claudeConfigFile.markdownDescription: Claude Code's global config file, read before the Claude Board starts a session, to warn when Claude has not trusted the folder yet (the session then opens so you can answer Claude's trust question). Written only by `#devdesk.worktrees.autoTrust#`, to trust a new worktree. Empty: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json`, else `~/.claude.json`.

devdesk.board.pasteSettleMs.markdownDescription: How long (ms) the Claude Board waits after pasting a command into a running session before it presses Enter, so Claude has taken the paste in (1 ms more per 4 KB pasted). Raise it if a sent command stays typed at the session's prompt instead of running.

devdesk.insights.enabled.markdownDescription: Ask a small model (`#devdesk.insights.model#`) what each Claude session is doing: a live status line on working cards, a short summary, and whether a finished turn waits for you (the 💬 asked look). Runs `claude -p --bare` next to your sessions, with your own Claude login; never touches the sessions themselves.

devdesk.insights.model.markdownDescription: The model insight calls use: an alias (`haiku`) or a full model name. Empty: `haiku`.

devdesk.insights.refreshSeconds.description: A working session's status is refreshed after new activity, at most this often (seconds).

devdesk.insights.maxConcurrent.description: How many insight calls run at the same time, across all sessions.

devdesk.insights.claudePath.markdownDescription: Claude Code binary insight calls run. Empty: the one new sessions run (`#devdesk.sessions.claudePath#`), without `#devdesk.sessions.claudeArgs#`.

devdesk.boardSearch.model.markdownDescription: The model the Claude Board's ✨ search asks (Enter in the search box), through `claude -p --bare` with your own Claude login. Empty: `haiku`. Not used when `#devdesk.boardSearch.command#` is set.

devdesk.boardSearch.command.markdownDescription: A program or script (with arguments) that answers the ✨ search instead of `claude -p`, for example a script around a local model (Ollama, llama.cpp). It is run in a login shell as `exec <command>`, so pipes or `;` need a wrapper script. It gets the search as JSON on stdin and prints `{"matches":[{"id":"…","reason":"…"}]}`; see the manual. A leading `~` is your home directory. Empty: `claude -p` with `#devdesk.boardSearch.model#`.

devdesk.boardSearch.timeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: How long a ✨ search may take before it is stopped.

devdesk.boardSearch.history.markdownDescription: Also search past Claude sessions (their transcripts) from the board's search box: matches show in a **Found in history** lane, and ✨ can pick them. The index stays on this machine, in `#devdesk.sessions.stateDir#`.

enumDescriptions: Sessions that ran in this workspace's folders and worktrees
Every Claude session on this machine
devdesk.boardSearch.historyScope.markdownDescription: Which past sessions the board's search looks through.

devdesk.boardSearch.historyDays.markdownDescription: Past sessions not changed for this many days are not searched.

devdesk.boardSearch.historyMaxSessions.markdownDescription: At most this many past sessions, the most recently changed, are searched. Each one indexed takes memory in the extension host (up to about 100 KB), so a folder with tens of thousands of transcripts (agents run with `claude -p`) is cut to the newest ones.

devdesk.boardSearch.historySaveMinutes.markdownDescription: How often (minutes) the window indexing past sessions saves the index file while they grow. This window's search sees new text at once; other windows see it once it is saved. It is also saved when the board closes, when sessions drop out of the index, and after reading a lot. 0: after every check (once a minute).

devdesk.boardSearch.historyDir.markdownDescription: Where Claude Code keeps its transcripts. Empty: `projects` in Claude's config directory (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`). A leading `~` is your home directory.

enumDescriptions: This window's project: its workspace, git repository or folder
All projects on this machine
devdesk.usage.defaultScope.markdownDescription: What the board's 📊 popup and the Claude Usage page show first, until you choose a project in them.

devdesk.usage.historyDays.markdownDescription: Days of token usage history kept for the Claude Board's 📊 and the Claude Usage page, after Claude Code deletes old transcripts (`cleanupPeriodDays`, 30 by default). Older days are dropped from `usage-history.jsonl` in `#devdesk.sessions.stateDir#`.

devdesk.usage.historyMaxMB.markdownDescription: The most disk space the token usage history may take (MB). Past it, the oldest days are dropped, whatever `#devdesk.usage.historyDays#` allows. A day takes a few KB.

devdesk.usage.planLimits.markdownDescription: Show how much of Claude's 5-hour and weekly plan limits you've used at the top of the board's 📊 popup and of the Claude Usage page (Claude.ai Pro and Max subscriptions). The numbers come from DevDesk's Claude status line (**Show Claude Plan Limits** command), which runs your own status line after it. While it isn't installed, they offer it; turn this off to hide that.

devdesk.cli.enabled.markdownDescription: Let Claude sessions ask this window to open a file or a diff, or set a note on their card, with the `devdesk` command (`~/.claude/devdesk/devdesk`, written when this is on; `devdesk --help`). Requests go through files in a folder only you can open, `~/.claude/devdesk/ipc`; no port is opened. To tell Claude the command exists, run **Claude: Teach Claude the devdesk Command**.

devdesk.workers.maxConcurrent.markdownDescription: The most worker sessions one coordinator may run at once with `devdesk worker start` (workers that reported, failed to start or ended don't count).

devdesk.workers.nudge.markdownDescription: When a coordinator session has unread worker messages and waits at an empty prompt, type a one-line notice into it ("You have N worker messages. Run `devdesk worker check`."), once per batch of messages. A busy session is never interrupted. Off: the coordinator reads them only when it runs `devdesk worker check`.

devdesk.workers.escalationMinutes.markdownDescription: Minutes a worker session may sit stopped (its turn over, or Claude gone) without `devdesk worker done` or `devdesk worker ask` before its coordinator gets a "stopped without reporting" message.

devdesk.sessions.tmuxServer.description: tmux server (tmux -L <name>) that DevDesk starts and lists Claude sessions on, kept apart from your own tmux. Empty means devdesk; "default" uses tmux's own server. Attach from a shell with: tmux -L devdesk attach.

devdesk.sessions.tmuxPath.markdownDescription: tmux binary DevDesk runs Claude sessions with, for example `~/.local/bin/tmux`. Empty: `tmux` on PATH. Another binary needs tmux 3.0 or later (DevDesk passes its path to the status hook with `new-session -e`).

devdesk.sessions.tmuxConfigFile.markdownDescription: tmux config file DevDesk's tmux server loads (`tmux -f <file>`), for example `~/.tmux-devdesk.conf`. Empty: DevDesk's own `tmux.conf` in `#devdesk.sessions.stateDir#`, which loads your tmux config (`~/.tmux.conf` and the others tmux reads) and then unsets its hooks, since they would also run for DevDesk's terminals, the board and the phone. With `#devdesk.sessions.tmuxServer#` set to `default`, empty means tmux's own config. tmux reads it when the server starts: run `tmux -L devdesk kill-server` (this stops every DevDesk session), or `source-file` it, to apply a change to a running server.

devdesk.sessions.smoothScroll.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Smoother mouse-wheel and trackpad scrolling in DevDesk's Claude terminals. With tmux's `mouse` on, tmux scrolls the terminal itself, 5 lines at a jump per wheel event; this makes each wheel event scroll `#devdesk.sessions.smoothScrollLines#` lines, one line at a time. It changes the wheel bindings of DevDesk's tmux server (all its sessions, in every window); turning it off gives back the bindings it replaced.

devdesk.sessions.smoothScrollLines.markdownDescription: With `#devdesk.sessions.smoothScroll#` on: lines one wheel event scrolls, one at a time. 3 scrolls about as far as VS Code's own terminal; 1 is the slowest and smoothest.

devdesk.sessions.tmuxOptions.markdownDescription: tmux options DevDesk sets on each Claude session when it opens its terminal (`set-option -t <session>`), for example `{ "mouse": true, "history-limit": 50000, "status": "off" }`. `true`/`false` become `on`/`off`. Window options apply to the session's current window. Empty: none, so your tmux config decides.

devdesk.sessions.tmuxInstallCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command **Install tmux** runs in a terminal, offered when DevDesk cannot run tmux. Empty: `brew install tmux` on macOS, else `sudo yum install -y tmux`.

devdesk.sessions.stateDir.description: Directory where the Claude status hook writes one JSON file per session.

devdesk.sessions.claudeSessionsDir.description: Directory where Claude Code lists its running sessions (`<pid>.json`), read for the names the agent view and /rename show. Empty means `sessions` in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude/sessions`.

devdesk.sessions.claudeJobsDir.description: Directory where Claude Code keeps its background jobs (`<job id>/state.json`), read to list the /fork forks of a listed session. Empty means `jobs` in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude/jobs`.

devdesk.diagnostics.debugLog.description: Write DevDesk's debug lines (tree loads, git and refresh timings) to the DevDesk output at info level, without changing VS Code's log level.

devdesk.diagnostics.slowOperationSeconds.description: Log a warning once when a DevDesk operation (git, tmux, a sessions refresh, a tree load) has been running this many seconds. 0 disables.

devdesk.diagnostics.latencyOutlierFactor.description: Log an info line when a command, a sessions refresh, a Claude Board render or a tmux call takes this many times as long as it usually does (its median of the last 50), with what else DevDesk was doing, so a slow moment can be debugged later. 0 disables.

devdesk.diagnostics.latencyOutlierMinMs.description: Only log a slow moment (devdesk.diagnostics.latencyOutlierFactor) that took at least this many milliseconds longer than usual.

devdesk.diagnostics.dir.description: Where the extension host writes a Node diagnostic report (native stack, heap spaces, resource usage) when it dies of a fatal error such as running out of memory. Empty: ~/.cache/devdesk/diagnostics.

devdesk.diagnostics.heapSnapshotNearLimi.description: Write one V8 heap snapshot (Heap.*.heapsnapshot, several GB) to the extension host's working directory when its heap nears the limit, to find which extension is allocating. Turning it off takes effect after a reload.

devdesk.diagnostics.keepDays.description: Delete heap snapshots (Heap.*.heapsnapshot in the extension host's working directory, usually ~) and fatal-error reports (in devdesk.diagnostics.dir) older than this many days. Checked when a window starts and every 6 hours. 0 keeps them.

devdesk.diagnostics.heapWarnMB.description: Log the extension host's memory every 10 s at info level (DevDesk output) once its heap is this big. 0 disables.

devdesk.diagnostics.heapGrowthWarnMB.description: Log a warning, with the DevDesk operations in flight, when the extension host's heap grows this much in 10 s. 0 disables.

devdesk.checks.enabled.description: Show each worktree's failing pull request checks and open review comments on its Worktrees view row and its sessions' board cards (`2 checks failing · 1 comment`), and offer Ask Claude to Fix Checks. GitHub pull requests are read with the `gh` CLI, when it is installed and signed in.

devdesk.checks.refreshMinutes.description: While the Worktrees view is visible, read a listed worktree's checks again at most this many minutes after the last time (on the view's refresh, `devdesk.worktrees.refreshSeconds`). 0: only when you ask Claude to fix them or run Refresh Pull Request Checks.

devdesk.checks.maxBackoffMinutes.description: After reading a worktree's checks fails (no `gh`, not signed in, no network), the next try waits twice as long each time, up to this many minutes.

devdesk.checks.timeoutSeconds.description: A `gh` call that takes longer is stopped.

devdesk.checks.reviewComments.description: Also read the pull request's review comments that aren't resolved yet, count them in the hint and put them (file, line, text) in the prompt to Claude.

devdesk.checks.logLines.description: Lines of a failing check's failed log (`gh run view --log-failed`) the prompt to Claude quotes: from the first line that looks like a failure to the last error. 0: no logs, only each check's link.

devdesk.checks.maxLogs.description: The failed logs of at most this many failing checks are read for one prompt; the others get their link only.

devdesk.checks.ghPath.description: The GitHub CLI to run. Empty: `gh` on PATH.

devdesk.tickets.enabled.description: Link tickets (issues) to worktrees and sessions, and show a chip with the ticket's key and status (`ABC-123 · In progress`) on the worktree's Worktrees view row and on its sessions' board cards. A click opens the ticket. Link one with Link Ticket… on a row or card.

devdesk.tickets.autoDetect.description: Find a worktree's ticket in its name and branch (`feat/ABC-123-login`, `issue-42`), and a session's in its first prompt, and link it. A ticket you unlink is not linked again automatically.

devdesk.tickets.includeInPrompt.description: Add the worktree's ticket (key, title, status, URL) after the prompt of each new session the board starts in that worktree.

devdesk.tickets.fetch.description: Read the title and status of linked tickets, read-only, where DevDesk can: GitHub issues with the `gh` CLI (`devdesk.checks.ghPath`), Jira with `devdesk.tickets.jira.command`. DevDesk keeps no tokens: the other trackers are link only.

devdesk.tickets.refreshMinutes.description: Read a linked ticket's title and status again at most this many minutes after the last time (a failure waits as long).

devdesk.tickets.timeoutSeconds.description: A ticket read (`gh issue view`, the Jira command) that takes longer is stopped.

devdesk.tickets.providers.markdownDescription: The trackers whose keys and links DevDesk recognises, by id: `github`, `jira`, `linear`, and `patterns` for every entry of `#devdesk.tickets.patterns#`. Empty: all of them.

devdesk.tickets.jira.baseUrl.markdownDescription: Your Jira site, such as `https://example.atlassian.net`. Set, keys like `ABC-123` and its `/browse/` links are Jira tickets. Empty: no Jira.

devdesk.tickets.jira.projects.markdownDescription: The Jira project keys (`ABC`) bare keys are taken for, in any case (branch names are often lowercase). Empty: any uppercase `ABC-123`, except words like `UTF-8` or `SHA-256`.

devdesk.tickets.jira.command.markdownDescription: A command that prints a Jira issue as JSON, to show its title and status: the key is in `$DEVDESK_TICKET`. For example `jira issue view "$DEVDESK_TICKET" --raw` (jira-cli), signed in on its own. Jira's REST fields (`fields.summary`, `fields.status.name`) or flat `title` and `status` are read. Empty: Jira tickets are link only.

devdesk.tickets.linear.workspace.markdownDescription: Your Linear workspace (the part after `linear.app/`). Set, keys like `ENG-123` link to its issues when Jira does not take them. Linear issue URLs are recognised either way. Link only.

devdesk.tickets.linear.teams.description: The Linear team keys (ENG) bare keys are taken for. Empty: any uppercase key.

name.description: The tracker's name, shown in hovers.

regex.description: A JavaScript regular expression for its keys or URLs; the first group is the key (else the whole match).

url.description: The ticket's URL: {key} is the key, {0} to {9} the regex's groups.

devdesk.tickets.patterns.markdownDescription: Trackers of your own, link only: each `{ "name", "regex", "url" }`, such as `{ "name": "Bugzilla", "regex": "\\bbug ?(\\d{4,})\\b", "url": "https://bugs.example.com/show_bug.cgi?id={key}" }`. They are asked before the built-in trackers.

enumDescriptions: devdesk.web.tunnelCommand when set, else the workspace kind's tunnel if it has one, else Start asks which tunnel to use.
Tailscale Serve (recommended): reachable only from devices on your tailnet; Tailscale names the visitor, who must be in devdesk.web.allowedUsers.
Microsoft Dev Tunnels: a private tunnel only your GitHub or Microsoft account can open. It names no one, so DevDesk checks no one itself: any process on this host can also use web access.

Cloudflare Tunnel behind Cloudflare Access: DevDesk checks Access's signed token (devdesk.web.cloudflare.team and .audience) and that its email is in devdesk.web.allowedUsers. Needs devdesk.web.publicHost.
ngrok, with its OAuth sign-in (devdesk.web.ngrok.oauthProvider) letting in only the emails in devdesk.web.allowedUsers.
devdesk.web.tunnelCommand, behind your own identity proxy (devdesk.web.identityHeader).
No tunnel: only 127.0.0.1 (through ssh -L, or a proxy you run yourself).
devdesk.web.tunnel.markdownDescription: Which tunnel takes web access to your phone. Run **Choose Web Access Tunnel** to set it up step by step. A preset runs its own command and identity check (`#devdesk.web.tunnelCommand#` and `#devdesk.web.identityHeader#` do not apply); `custom` runs `#devdesk.web.tunnelCommand#`. Ignored with `#devdesk.web.auth#` `loopback`.

devdesk.web.port.markdownDescription: Port the web access daemon listens on, on `127.0.0.1` only (there is no setting for the address: reach it through a proxy or `ssh -L`). 1024 to 65535.

enumDescriptions: A request is allowed only when the proxy's identity header (devdesk.web.identityHeader) names one of devdesk.web.allowedUsers. Missing either: every request is denied.

No identity check, for ssh -L: any process on this host can then open the page and drive your Claude sessions. Use it only on a host no one else uses. Web access then answers on 127.0.0.1 and localhost only, and does not start with devdesk.web.tunnelCommand or devdesk.web.publicHost set.
devdesk.web.auth.markdownDescription: How web access decides who may use it. `header` (default): the identity proxy in front of it must set `#devdesk.web.identityHeader#` to one of `#devdesk.web.allowedUsers#`; when either is missing, every request is denied. `loopback`: no identity check, for `ssh -L`; any process on this host can then drive Claude. It answers on `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` only, and does not start with `#devdesk.web.tunnelCommand#` or `#devdesk.web.publicHost#` set.

devdesk.web.identityHeader.markdownDescription: HTTP header the identity proxy sets to the signed-in visitor (for example `Tailscale-User-Login` or `Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email`); the proxy must remove any value the browser sends. Empty: the workspace kind's header when its default tunnel command runs, else none (every request is denied).

devdesk.web.allowedUsers.markdownDescription: Who may use web access, matched exactly (case and spaces count): your Tailscale login, or your email for `cloudflare` and `ngrok`, or the values of `#devdesk.web.identityHeader#` your proxy sets. **Choose Web Access Tunnel** fills it in. Empty: your user name when the workspace kind's default tunnel command runs, else none (every request is denied). Not used by `devtunnel`.

devdesk.web.publicHost.markdownDescription: Host name (`host` or `host:port`) the proxy serves web access on; requests for any other host than this and `127.0.0.1` are refused. Needed for the `cloudflare` tunnel (the host its DNS route and Access application use); for `ngrok`, your reserved domain. Empty: taken from the URL the tunnel command prints.

devdesk.web.tunnelName.patternErrorMessage: Use at most 24 letters, digits and dashes.
devdesk.web.tunnelName.markdownDescription: This machine's part of the tunnel's name (`{host}` in the tunnel command), so each machine gets a tunnel and URL of its own: for example `mac` on your laptop and `cloud` on a cloud machine. Lower case, at most 24 letters, digits and dashes. Empty: this machine's short host name. [Set Web Access Tunnel Name](command:devdesk.web.setTunnelName) shows the tunnel name and URL a name gives as you type; so does the **Tunnel name** row in the Web Access view.

devdesk.web.tunnelCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command that exposes the port through an identity proxy, run after the daemon starts when `#devdesk.web.tunnel#` is `custom` (or `auto`), with `{port}`, `{user}`, `{host}` (`#devdesk.web.tunnelName#`, else this machine's short host name) and `{publicHost}` filled in. The first `https://` URL it prints is the URL to open on the phone. Empty: the workspace kind's default, if any, else no tunnel (run your proxy yourself).

devdesk.web.pollMs.markdownDescription: How often, in milliseconds, the web page's session list is refreshed while it is open. 500 to 60000.

devdesk.web.cloudflare.team.markdownDescription: For the `cloudflare` tunnel: your Cloudflare One team name (`<team>.cloudflareaccess.com`). Empty: every request is denied.

devdesk.web.cloudflare.audience.markdownDescription: For the `cloudflare` tunnel: the Application Audience (AUD) Tag of the Access application in front of `#devdesk.web.publicHost#`. Empty: every request is denied.

devdesk.web.ngrok.oauthProvider.markdownDescription: For the `ngrok` tunnel: the account visitors sign in with; only the emails in `#devdesk.web.allowedUsers#` get through.

enumDescriptions: The transcript, the screen, and a reply box.
Experimental: the session's live terminal, as on your desktop. While you type on the phone, the session's window takes the phone's size; it takes your desktop's back when you type there.
devdesk.web.sessionView.markdownDescription: What the web page shows when you open a session. Each browser can choose its own in the page's settings (the gear); this is what a browser that didn't choose gets.
